rows.component_basis: La2O3 formula-unit mole fraction as x_La2O3 approaches zero; Li et al.'s RK x1 is inferred to use one La2O3 oxide formula unit per component unit; k=1
rows.parent_standard_state: pure liquid La2O3(l), 1 bar; liquid Raoult standard, metastable at 1873 K

flag_labels.melt_family_extrapolated: The composition contains oxides outside the assessed SiO2-La2O3 binary edge.

rows.source_locator: Eq. (1), p. 2; Eq. (2), p. 4; Table 2 La2O3-SiO2 parameters, p. 6; section 3.1.3, p. 9
limitations: assessed phase-diagram fit; not a measured activity. Li et al. report that the La2O3-SiO2 interaction parameters were optimized against phase-diagram data from Toropov (1961) and Bondar (1982).
uncertainty not stated: Table 2 gives no parameter-fit uncertainty, so the evaluated point is also the band at both endpoints.
Provisional, infinite-dilution La2O3 formula-unit limit only; no finite-loading cutoff is reported.
The operational 1773-1873 K window follows the assessed liquid-region work at 1500 and 1600 degrees C; the paper gives no coefficient-fit temperature bounds.

The evaluated coefficient is the SiO2-edge infinite-dilution limit. Li et al.'s ternary Kohler model with its added -450000*x_La2O3*x_Al2O3*x_SiO2^2 term makes gamma_infinity depend on the Al2O3:SiO2 solvent ratio: at 1873 K it is about 9.8e-6 at x_SiO2=5/6 (19 times below this binary value) and about 1.5e-3 in pure Al2O3 (8 times above it). Any Al2O3 therefore raises the family-extrapolation flag. No CaO/MgO/FeO interaction is modeled, so the bias direction for those basic-melt extrapolations is unknown. For Al2O3-bearing melts, the bias direction depends on the solvent ratio.
